title: Scale governor: metric sentinel, hybrid-signal scaling, and failsafe envelope
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets need predictable throughput guarantees while avoiding costly overscale and unsafe rapid oscillation. Current heuristics react to single metrics (p50 latency or avg throughput) and can either overprovision or cause repeated step changes leading to KV cache warmup penalties and customer-visible latency spikes.

Goal: Ship a scale governor component that composes multiple signals (percentile latency, token throughput, queue depth, warm-cache ratio) into a hybrid target metric, applies a gradient-clamped scaling algorithm, and enforces a failsafe envelope (rapid-shed, slow-surge, rollback fences) per-fleet and per-tenant. The feature should provide observability, simulation harness, and a safe rollout path with policy overrides for enterprise tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Scale governor accepts a policy definition that references 3 signal groups: latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), token/sec over 1m and 5m, and steady-state KV cache hit ratio.
Scaling algorithm produces step decisions limited by configurable 'max_pct_step' and 'min_interstep_seconds' and logs rationales for each decision to the console trace.

A failsafe envelope implements: (a) surge_slowdown windows to limit new upscales during high-error periods, (b) rollback_fence to revert a recent scale within N minutes if error rate increases by X%, (c) emergency_shed policy to honor throughput guarantees by shedding lower-priority tenants when necessary.

End-to-end integration tests demonstrate stable behavior across three synthetic workloads (spiky, ramp, and steady burst) with less than 10% overshoot compared to target capacity and no oscillation loops longer than 3 steps.
Telemetry surfaces per-decision signal weights, simulated counterfactuals (what-if for alternate action), and a scoring field used for debugging in Console and runtime logs.
Feature gated behind runtime-flag and rolled out initially to canary fleet with SLA-backed tenants excluded from automatic shedding.
Design doc and policy DSL examples reviewed and approved by PM and Security; security_review_required set to 'true' for key-management of policy overrides.
design_notes: We will use a hybrid signal model: composite_score = w1*norm(p95_latency) + w2*norm(throughput_gap) + w3*(1 - kv_hit_ratio). We store recent normalization params in per-fleet counters to adapt to workload baselines.

Scaling decisions computed every 30s by default with a configurable control window. To avoid oscillation, we clamp fractional scale recommendations to N% of current capacity and apply an exponential decay to successive upscales within short windows.

Introduce a lightweight credit ledger (tokenized headroom) that grants ephemeral burst credits to tenants; credits decay and are replenished based on historical underutilization. Credits are accounted in the decision rationale and visible in Console.

Failsafe envelope semantics: define three orthogonal fences — magnitude fence (max_pct_step), time fence (min_interstep_seconds), and contextual fence (do-not-scale-during-degradation=true). Contextual fence uses error trend detection to prevent aggressive upscales during ongoing infra incidents.

Policy DSL prototype: human-readable YAML with rule precedence. Example: 'scale_if: composite_score > threshold for 2 consecutive windows; action: scale_up by computed_pct limited_by max_pct_step; rollback_if: error_rate increases > 20% within 10m'.

Trade-offs considered: heavier signal composition reduces sensitivity to noisy metric spikes but adds complexity to reasoning and debugging. We mitigate with per-decision rationale logging and a 'what-if' sim endpoint.

Interaction with KV cache: we prefer slower, larger upscales over frequent tiny ones to reduce cache churn; add a cache-warmup score that penalizes scaling decisions if predicted warmup cost exceeds threshold.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit tests and simulation harness; internal runtime flag enabled in dev clusters.
Phase 1 (canary): enable on 5% of Dedicated fleets (non-SLA tenants) for 48h. Monitor decision logs and 'what-if' simulation mismatches.
Phase 2 (pilot): expand to 20% of fleets including one mid-enterprise tenant with manual override; collect performance and cost delta over 2 weeks.
Phase 3 (gradual): opt-in for all fleets with default policy, enterprise tenants may pin to legacy behavior until signed-off. Toggle emergency_shed default to 'off' for enterprise customers.
Rollback: runtime flag flip; automated rollback if oscillation metric exceeds threshold or customer-impacting latency regressions detected.
testing_plan: Unit tests for composite_score calculation, including normalization edge cases (stale baselines, division by zero).
Integration tests mocking telemetry streams (latency, throughput, kv hits) verifying step limits and rollback fences.
Chaos experiments: inject transient infra errors and ensure contextual fence prevents harmful upscales.
Load sims: spiky, ramp, and plateau profiles; assert <10% overshoot and no >3-step oscillation loops.
End-to-end experiment: apply to canary fleet and compare billing delta vs. legacy autoscaler for 2 weeks.
monitoring: Per-decision log: timestamp, composite_score, component contributions (p95, throughput_gap, kv_penalty), computed_action, clamped_action, rationale_code.
Dashboard panels: decision rate, average step size, oscillation count, rollback events, emergency_shed invocations, cost delta vs baseline.
Alerting: high oscillation rate (>5 oscillation events per hour), repeated rollback_fence triggers, >15% unexpected cost increase in 1h window.
SLOs: maintain 99.9% fleet availability; limit mean 95th latency regression to <5% against baseline for rollout windows.
